Using a fresh bogus name each time lets X keep erasing the lock, so the attacker gets unlimited guesses at about 1 per second per process. Lockouts also never escalate.
3. Stale processes also undo an administrator's `unlock`/`reset` and miss password resets. `CredentialStore` is also loaded once (lines 396-413), so a login process started before an administrator resets a compromised password still accepts the old password.

This defeats the core requirement in `prompt.txt` and contradicts README points 5 and 6.

**Fix:** Serialise the check-verify-record sequence across processes with an OS-level exclusive file lock. Inside that lock, reload the lockout and credential state from disk, so every decision and every write uses the current on-disk state. Administrator commands must take the same lock and reload before `save`/`reset`. Sleep after releasing the lock. For multi-server deployments, move the state into a transactional database and use an atomic conditional update (for example `UPDATE ... SET failures = failures + 1 ... RETURNING`, or `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`).
```java
import java.nio.channels.FileChannel;
import java.nio.channels.FileLock;

// In LoginAttemptTracker (and the same for CredentialStore): move the parsing loop out of the
// constructor into parse(file) and expose reload(), so each attempt works on the on-disk state.
synchronized void reload() throws IOException {
    Map<String, AccountState> fresh = parse(file);   // same parsing and fail-closed checks as today
    states.clear();
    states.putAll(fresh);
}

// In Authenticator: lockFile = dataDir.resolve("portal.lock"), passed in from main().
AuthOutcome authenticate(String rawUsername, char[] password) throws IOException {
    String username = normalizeUsername(rawUsername);
    if (username == null) {
        PasswordHasher.verify(password, dummySalt, PasswordHasher.ITERATIONS, dummyHash);
        audit.record("LOGIN_FAILED_MALFORMED_USERNAME", null);
        pauseAfterFailure();
        return new AuthOutcome(AuthStatus.INVALID_CREDENTIALS, null, null);
    }

    AuthOutcome outcome;
    // One exclusive OS-level lock shared by every process that uses this data directory.
    try (FileChannel channel = FileChannel.open(lockFile, StandardOpenOption.CREATE, StandardOpenOption.WRITE);
         FileLock ignored = channel.lock()) {
        tracker.reload();   // see failures and lockouts written by other processes
        store.reload();     // see password resets and new accounts
        LoginAttemptTracker.AccountState state = tracker.stateFor(username);
        synchronized (state) {
            // Existing body: activeLockout -> verify -> recordSuccess/recordFailure (which persists),
            // without the pauseAfterFailure() call.
            outcome = checkVerifyAndRecord(username, password, state);
        }
    }
    if (outcome.status() != AuthStatus.SUCCESS) {
        pauseAfterFailure();   // after releasing the lock, so other accounts are not blocked
    }
    return outcome;
}
```

### SEC-02: Administrator commands (password reset, unlock) require no authentication
- **Severity:** High
- **CWE:** CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function
- **Location:** `EmployeePortalAuth.java:103-108`, `EmployeePortalAuth.java:169-213`

**Vulnerable code:**
```java
// EmployeePortalAuth.java:103-108
            if (args.length == 0) {
                runLogin(terminal, authenticator);
            } else if (args.length == 2 && args[0].equals("add-user")) {
                runAddUser(terminal, store, tracker, audit, args[1]);
            } else if (args.length == 2 && args[0].equals("unlock")) {
                runUnlock(terminal, tracker, audit, args[1]);

// EmployeePortalAuth.java:188-191
            boolean existed = store.find(username).isPresent();
            store.save(UserRecord.create(username, first));
            tracker.reset(username);
            audit.record(existed ? "PASSWORD_RESET" : "USER_CREATED", username);
```

**Why it is a problem:** The login program and the administrator functions share one entry point and one data directory. To log anyone in, the process must be able to read `users.db` and write `lockouts.db`, so whatever OS identity runs the login also has everything `add-user` needs. The code performs no administrator check: no admin credential, no role, no OS group check. `add-user <existing name>` silently replaces the victim's password and clears the lockout. Anyone who can start the program with arguments (a shell as the portal service account, a wrapper or sudo rule that passes arguments through, a kiosk script that forwards input) can run `java EmployeePortalAuth add-user ceo`, choose a new password, and log in as that employee. `unlock` lets an attacker clear lockouts between guessing rounds, which also defeats the brute-force control. The "(administrator)" labels in the usage text and README are documentation only.

**Fix:** Take administrative operations out of the login entry point. Give them a separate program that is installed so only administrators can run it, and that re-authenticates an administrator account listed in a roster the login identity cannot modify. Audit the acting administrator as well as the target account.
```java
// EmployeePortalAuth.main: the login entry point accepts no arguments at all.
public static void main(String[] args) {
    if (args.length != 0) {
        System.err.println("Usage: java EmployeePortalAuth");
        System.exit(2);
    }
    Path dataDir = resolveDataDir();
    Terminal terminal = new Terminal();
    try {
        Storage.ensurePrivateDirectory(dataDir);
        CredentialStore store = new CredentialStore(dataDir.resolve("users.db"));
        LoginAttemptTracker tracker =
                new LoginAttemptTracker(dataDir.resolve("lockouts.db"), Clock.systemUTC());
        AuditLog audit = new AuditLog(dataDir.resolve("audit.log"), Clock.systemUTC());
        runLogin(terminal, new Authenticator(store, tracker, audit));
    } catch (IOException | UncheckedIOException e) {
        System.err.println("Error: the portal records could not be read or written: " + e.getMessage());
        System.exit(1);
    }
}

// EmployeePortalAdmin.java: separate class, installed executable only by the portal-admins group.
// The admin roster (admins.txt) is owned by root and not writable by the login service account.
static void requireAdministrator(Terminal terminal, Authenticator authenticator, Set<String> adminRoster,
                                 AuditLog audit) throws IOException {
    String admin = terminal.readLine("Administrator username: ");
    char[] pw = terminal.readPassword("Administrator password: ");
    AuthOutcome outcome;
    try {
        outcome = authenticator.authenticate(admin, pw == null ? new char[0] : pw);
    } finally {
        if (pw != null) {
            Arrays.fill(pw, '\0');
        }
    }
    if (outcome.status() != AuthStatus.SUCCESS || !adminRoster.contains(outcome.username())) {
        audit.record("ADMIN_AUTH_FAILED", outcome.username());
        System.exit(1);
    }
    audit.record("ADMIN_AUTH_OK", outcome.username());
}
```

### SEC-03: Permissions of a pre-existing data directory and its files are not verified
- **Severity:** Medium
- **CWE:** CWE-732: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
- **Location:** `EmployeePortalAuth.java:602-609`

**Vulnerable code:**
```java
// EmployeePortalAuth.java:602-609
        static void ensurePrivateDirectory(Path dir) throws IOException {
            if (Files.notExists(dir)) {
                Files.createDirectories(dir);
                if (posix(dir)) {
                    Files.setPosixFilePermissions(dir, PosixFilePermissions.fromString("rwx------"));
                }
            }
        }
```

**Why it is a problem:** Permissions are only restricted when the program creates the directory itself. If the directory already exists, the program uses it as-is. That covers the README's `/srv/portal/auth` example created with `mkdir`, a group-writable directory, a directory in a shared location, or a symbolic link. Pre-existing `users.db` and `lockouts.db` files are also not checked. The consequences:
- If group or others can write to the directory, they can rename, delete or replace `users.db` even when the file itself is `0600`, because unlinking and renaming depend on the directory's permissions. Replacing it with their own hash for any username gives account takeover. Deleting `lockouts.db` clears every lockout. They can also plant a symlink named `audit.log`, which gets followed at lines 580-583.
- If `users.db` was created or copied with `0644`, every local user can read the password hashes and crack them offline. The file is only rewritten as `0600` when an administrator saves, never during login.

The README states "Only the user who runs the program can open it", but the code does not enforce this.

**Fix:** Create the directory with owner-only permissions atomically. Reject symbolic links and non-directories. Refuse to start if the directory or any existing data file is accessible to group or others. Tightening permissions silently is not enough, because tampering may already have happened.
```java
static void ensurePrivateDirectory(Path dir) throws IOException {
    if (Files.notExists(dir, LinkOption.NOFOLLOW_LINKS)) {
        if (posix(dir)) {
            Files.createDirectories(dir,
                    PosixFilePermissions.asFileAttribute(PosixFilePermissions.fromString("rwx------")));
        } else {
            Files.createDirectories(dir);
        }
    }
    if (!Files.isDirectory(dir, LinkOption.NOFOLLOW_LINKS)) {
        throw new IOException(dir + " is not a directory (symbolic links are not accepted)");
    }
    requireOwnerOnly(dir);
    for (String name : List.of("users.db", "lockouts.db", "audit.log")) {
        Path f = dir.resolve(name);
        if (Files.exists(f, LinkOption.NOFOLLOW_LINKS)) {
            if (!Files.isRegularFile(f, LinkOption.NOFOLLOW_LINKS)) {
                throw new IOException(f + " is not a regular file");
            }
            requireOwnerOnly(f);
        }
    }
}

private static void requireOwnerOnly(Path p) throws IOException {
    if (!posix(p)) {
        return;
    }
    Set<PosixFilePermission> perms = Files.getPosixFilePermissions(p, LinkOption.NOFOLLOW_LINKS);
    for (PosixFilePermission perm : perms) {
        if (perm.name().startsWith("GROUP_") || perm.name().startsWith("OTHERS_")) {
            throw new IOException(p + " must not be accessible to group or others (found "
                    + PosixFilePermissions.toString(perms) + ")");
        }
    }
}
```

### SEC-04: Lockout records for arbitrary usernames are never pruned, so state grows without limit
- **Severity:** Medium
- **CWE:** CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
- **Location:** `EmployeePortalAuth.java:484-487`, `EmployeePortalAuth.java:446-448`, `EmployeePortalAuth.java:546-552`

**Vulnerable code:**
```java
// EmployeePortalAuth.java:484-487
        /** Returns the single shared state object for a username. It is never removed from the map. */
        AccountState stateFor(String username) {
            return states.computeIfAbsent(username, k -> new AccountState());
        }

// EmployeePortalAuth.java:546-552
            states.entrySet().stream().sorted(Map.Entry.comparingByKey()).forEach(e -> {
                AccountState s = e.getValue();
                if (!s.isClear()) {
                    lines.add(e.getKey() + ":" + s.consecutiveFailures + ":" + s.lockoutCount + ":"
                            + s.lockedUntilMillis + ":" + s.lastFailureMillis);
                }
            });
```

**Why it is a problem:** To avoid user enumeration, every well-formed username gets tracked, including names that don't exist. After a single failed attempt, `consecutiveFailures` is non-zero, so the entry is written to `lockouts.db`. Entries are never removed. Once a lock has expired and the 24-hour escalation window has passed, `lockoutCount` and `lockedUntilMillis` stay non-zero, so `isClear()` stays false forever. Only a successful login or an administrator reset clears an entry, and neither happens for made-up usernames. An attacker who submits random 64-character usernames adds one permanent line per attempt, from as many processes as they like. Every failed attempt then sorts the whole map and rewrites the whole file (lines 543-554), and every process start parses it all (lines 459-480). Login latency and disk use grow without bound until startup becomes very slow or the disk fills. A full disk makes `persist()` fail, which exits the program, so no one can log in.

**Fix:** Treat entries whose lock has expired and whose escalation window has passed as clear. Such an entry already behaves exactly like a fresh state in `recordFailure` and `activeLockout`, so drop it on load and on persist. Enforce a hard limit on file size and alert when it is reached.
```java
/** True when the entry can no longer affect any decision: no active lock and the escalation window has passed. */
static boolean isExpired(AccountState s, long now) {
    long quietSince = Math.max(s.lastFailureMillis, s.lockedUntilMillis);
    return now >= s.lockedUntilMillis && now - quietSince > ESCALATION_RESET_WINDOW.toMillis();
}

private synchronized void persist() {
    long now = clock.millis();
    List<String> lines = new ArrayList<>();
    lines.add("# Employee portal lockout state. Format: username:failures:lockouts:lockedUntil:lastFailure");
    states.entrySet().stream().sorted(Map.Entry.comparingByKey()).forEach(e -> {
        AccountState s = e.getValue();
        if (!s.isClear() && !isExpired(s, now)) {
            lines.add(e.getKey() + ":" + s.consecutiveFailures + ":" + s.lockoutCount + ":"
                    + s.lockedUntilMillis + ":" + s.lastFailureMillis);
        }
    });
    if (lines.size() > MAX_TRACKED_ACCOUNTS) {   // e.g. 100_000; alert operators, fail closed
        throw new UncheckedIOException(new IOException("lockout state exceeds " + MAX_TRACKED_ACCOUNTS + " entries"));
    }
    try {
        Storage.writeAtomically(file, lines);
    } catch (IOException e) {
        throw new UncheckedIOException("could not save lockout state", e);
    }
}

// In the loading loop (constructor / reload), skip entries that are already expired:
//     if (!isExpired(s, clock.millis())) { states.put(p[0], s); }
```

### SEC-05: Credential store location comes from the caller's environment or working directory
- **Severity:** Low
- **CWE:** CWE-15: External Control of System or Configuration Setting
- **Location:** `EmployeePortalAuth.java:122-131`

**Vulnerable code:**
```java
// EmployeePortalAuth.java:122-131
    private static Path resolveDataDir() {
        String dir = System.getProperty("portal.dataDir");
        if (dir == null || dir.isBlank()) {
            dir = System.getenv("PORTAL_DATA_DIR");
        }
        if (dir == null || dir.isBlank()) {
            dir = "portal-data";
        }
        return Paths.get(dir);
    }
```

**Why it is a problem:** The source of truth for authentication (which accounts exist, their hashes, and their lockout state) is chosen by whoever controls the process environment or the working directory. The default is a relative path, so running the program from a different directory silently creates an empty, separate store. That drops all lockouts, and administrator changes end up in the wrong store. If a wrapper passes the caller's environment through, or runs the program from a user-controlled directory, the caller can point `PORTAL_DATA_DIR` at a directory containing their own `users.db` and "authenticate" as anyone. The login decision then no longer reflects the real records.

**Fix:** Use a fixed absolute path owned by the portal service account, or read it from a root-owned configuration file. Do not accept overrides from the environment or relative paths in production builds.
```java
/** Fixed location owned by the portal service account; never taken from the caller's environment. */
static final Path DATA_DIR = Paths.get("/var/lib/employee-portal");

private static Path resolveDataDir() {
    if (!DATA_DIR.isAbsolute()) {
        throw new IllegalStateException("data directory must be absolute");
    }
    return DATA_DIR;
}
```

### SEC-06: Anyone can lock any known account for up to 24 hours
- **Severity:** Low
- **CWE:** CWE-645: Overly Restrictive Account Lockout Mechanism
- **Location:** `EmployeePortalAuth.java:61-68`, `EmployeePortalAuth.java:505-509`

**Vulnerable code:**
```java
// EmployeePortalAuth.java:61-68
    /** Consecutive failed attempts allowed before the account is locked. */
    static final int MAX_CONSECUTIVE_FAILURES = 5;

    /** Length of the first lockout. Each further lockout doubles, up to MAX_LOCKOUT. */
    static final Duration BASE_LOCKOUT = Duration.ofMinutes(15);

    /** Upper limit for any single lockout. */
    static final Duration MAX_LOCKOUT = Duration.ofHours(24);

// EmployeePortalAuth.java:505-509
            if (s.consecutiveFailures >= MAX_CONSECUTIVE_FAILURES) {
                s.lockedUntilMillis = now + lockoutDuration(s.lockoutCount).toMillis();
                s.lockoutCount = s.lockoutCount + 1;
                s.consecutiveFailures = 0;
            }
```

**Why it is a problem:** No credential is needed to lock an account. Five wrong passwords for a username lock it. Repeating the 5 attempts each time a lock expires escalates to 24-hour locks (15 min, 30 min, … 16 h, 24 h). Usernames follow an obvious pattern (`jsmith`), so one person can lock out a whole department or a specific administrator, and a correct password is refused during the lock. The README acknowledges this, but the only recovery is a manual administrator `unlock`, which SEC-01 and SEC-02 show is itself weak.

**Fix:** Use a hard lock that is short and capped, and prefer throttling (rising delays) over long lockouts, following NIST SP 800-63B §5.2.2. Alert on repeated lockouts so the attack is visible. Where possible, offer a second factor so a legitimate user can unlock themselves.
```java
/** Consecutive failed attempts allowed before the account is temporarily locked. */
static final int MAX_CONSECUTIVE_FAILURES = 10;

/** Short first lock; each further lock doubles, capped so a malicious lockout cannot last a working day. */
static final Duration BASE_LOCKOUT = Duration.ofMinutes(1);
static final Duration MAX_LOCKOUT = Duration.ofMinutes(30);

// in recordFailure, after applying a lock:
if (s.lockoutCount >= 3) {
    audit.record("ALERT_REPEATED_LOCKOUT", username);   // forward to monitoring / SIEM
}
```

### SEC-07: No per-session or cross-account throttling, which allows password spraying
- **Severity:** Low
- **CWE:** CWE-307: Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts
- **Location:** `EmployeePortalAuth.java:133-136`, `EmployeePortalAuth.java:161-165`

**Vulnerable code:**
```java
// EmployeePortalAuth.java:133-136
    private static void runLogin(Terminal terminal, Authenticator authenticator) throws IOException {
        terminal.println("=== Employee Portal Login ===");
        while (true) {
            String username = terminal.readLine("Username (leave blank to quit): ");

// EmployeePortalAuth.java:161-165
                case INVALID_CREDENTIALS:
                default:
                    terminal.println("Access denied. Invalid username or password.");
                    break;
            }
```

**Why it is a problem:** All limits are per account. One session can loop forever, trying `Winter2026!!` or other common passwords against every username at 1 attempt per second (4 guesses per account before a lock) without ever triggering a lockout. Across many parallel sessions the total rate is unbounded. The program has no global failed-login rate limit and no per-session attempt cap, so password spraying and credential stuffing with leaked lists go unchecked. This is the attack the README admits the design does not stop.

**Fix:** End the session after a few failures, whichever accounts they were against. Add a global failed-attempt rate limit, stored under the same cross-process lock as SEC-01, that slows every login when it is exceeded. For anything reachable outside a trusted network, add MFA.
```java
private static final int MAX_FAILURES_PER_SESSION = 3;

private static void runLogin(Terminal terminal, Authenticator authenticator) throws IOException {
    terminal.println("=== Employee Portal Login ===");
    int sessionFailures = 0;
    while (sessionFailures < MAX_FAILURES_PER_SESSION) {
        String username = terminal.readLine("Username (leave blank to quit): ");
        if (username == null || username.isBlank()) {
            terminal.println("Goodbye.");
            return;
        }
        char[] password = terminal.readPassword("Password: ");
        if (password == null) {
            return;
        }
        AuthOutcome outcome;
        try {
            outcome = authenticator.authenticate(username, password);   // also enforces a global failure-rate limit
        } finally {
            Arrays.fill(password, '\0');
        }
        if (outcome.status() == AuthStatus.SUCCESS) {
            terminal.println("Access granted. Welcome, " + outcome.username() + ".");
            return;
        }
        sessionFailures++;
        terminal.println(outcome.status() == AuthStatus.LOCKED_OUT
                ? "Access denied. Too many failed attempts. This account is locked until "
                        + TIME_FORMAT.format(outcome.lockedUntil()) + "."
                : "Access denied. Invalid username or password.");
    }
    terminal.println("Too many failed attempts in this session.");
}
```

### SEC-08: PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 iteration count below current guidance, with no rehash on login
- **Severity:** Low
- **CWE:** CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort
- **Location:** `EmployeePortalAuth.java:317-320`, `EmployeePortalAuth.java:381-383`

**Vulnerable code:**
```java
// EmployeePortalAuth.java:317-320
        static final String ALGORITHM = "PBKDF2WithHmacSHA256";
        static final int ITERATIONS = 210_000;
        static final int MIN_ITERATIONS = 10_000;
        static final int MAX_ITERATIONS = 5_000_000;
```

**Why it is a problem:** 210,000 iterations is the OWASP Password Storage Cheat Sheet figure for PBKDF2-HMAC-**SHA512**. For PBKDF2-HMAC-**SHA256** the recommendation is 600,000. If `users.db` is stolen (see SEC-03), cracking costs about 3× less than recommended. Records with as few as 10,000 iterations are also accepted (lines 381-383) and never upgraded, so legacy or tampered-in weak hashes stay weak forever.

**Fix:** Raise the work factor. On every successful login, transparently rehash any record below the current count, under the cross-process lock from SEC-01 so the save cannot overwrite concurrent administrator changes. Consider Argon2id (via a vetted library) for memory hardness.
```java
static final String ALGORITHM = "PBKDF2WithHmacSHA256";
static final int ITERATIONS = 600_000;          // OWASP guidance for PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256
static final int MIN_ITERATIONS = 100_000;      // older records are still readable, then upgraded
static final int MAX_ITERATIONS = 5_000_000;

// In Authenticator.authenticate, inside the lock, when the password is valid:
if (valid && record.get().iterations() < PasswordHasher.ITERATIONS) {
    store.save(UserRecord.create(username, password));   // rehash with the current work factor
}
```

### SEC-09: Password policy checks length only, with no blocklist
- **Severity:** Low
- **CWE:** CWE-521: Weak Password Requirements
- **Location:** `EmployeePortalAuth.java:183-187`

**Vulnerable code:**
```java
// EmployeePortalAuth.java:183-187
            if (first.length < MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH || first.length > MAX_PASSWORD_LENGTH) {
                terminal.println("Passwords must be between " + MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH + " and "
                        + MAX_PASSWORD_LENGTH + " characters. No changes were made.");
                System.exit(2);
            }
```

**Why it is a problem:** Any 12-character string is accepted, including `passwordpassword`, `123456789012`, `Company2026!`, or the username repeated. The main defence left against the spraying in SEC-07 is that passwords must not be common, and nothing checks for that. NIST SP 800-63B requires checking new passwords against known-breached and commonly used values and context-specific words.

**Fix:** Reject passwords found in a breached or common-password blocklist, and passwords that contain the username or the portal or company name. Keep the length limits.
```java
if (first.length < MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH || first.length > MAX_PASSWORD_LENGTH) {
    terminal.println("Passwords must be between " + MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH + " and "
            + MAX_PASSWORD_LENGTH + " characters. No changes were made.");
    System.exit(2);
}
String candidate = new String(first).toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT);
// PasswordBlocklist loads a breached/common password list (e.g. a top-100k list) from a read-only resource.
if (PasswordBlocklist.contains(candidate)
        || candidate.contains(username)
        || candidate.contains("portal")
        || candidate.chars().distinct().count() < 5) {
    terminal.println("That password is too common or too easy to guess. No changes were made.");
    System.exit(2);
}
```

## 6. Verified Controls and Checks With No Finding
- **Password hashing algorithm and salt:** PBKDF2WithHmacSHA256 with a 256-bit derived key and a per-user 16-byte salt from a shared `SecureRandom` (`EmployeePortalAuth.java:316-332`, `364-368`). No MD5/SHA-1, no unsalted hashing, no predictable RNG. Only the iteration count is flagged (SEC-08).
- **Constant-time comparison:** `MessageDigest.isEqual` is used for the hash comparison (`EmployeePortalAuth.java:352`).
- **Hardcoded secrets:** No passwords, keys, tokens or default accounts in the source, README or metadata files.
- **Username enumeration:** Every bad username or password gets the same message (`EmployeePortalAuth.java:161-164`). Unknown and malformed usernames still run a full PBKDF2 against a random dummy hash (`254`, `281`). Unknown usernames are tracked and locked like real ones (`260-262`), so lockout messages don't reveal which accounts exist. The account lookup happens only after the lock check (`266-275`).
- **No password verification while locked:** A locked account is rejected before the password is checked (`EmployeePortalAuth.java:267-273`), so a correct guess during a lock reveals nothing.
- **In-process concurrency:** Within one JVM, the check-verify-record sequence runs under a per-account monitor that is never removed (`266`, `485-487`), and `persist()` is synchronized (`543`). Lock ordering (account, then tracker) is consistent in `authenticate` and `reset` (`526-534`), so no deadlock. Cross-process behaviour is the problem (SEC-01).
- **Fail-closed state handling:** A failure to persist lockout state stops the process without granting access (`EmployeePortalAuth.java:553-558`, `116-119`). Malformed `lockouts.db` or `users.db` lines stop startup instead of being skipped (`476-479`, `408-410`).
- **Lockout arithmetic:** The escalation shift is capped at 20 and the duration at `MAX_LOCKOUT`, so there is no overflow (`EmployeePortalAuth.java:537-541`).
- **Input validation / injection into files and logs (CWE-117, CWE-93):** Usernames are normalised and must match `^[a-z0-9._-]{1,64}$` (`80`, `242-248`) before they are used in the `:`-delimited stores or the audit log. Malformed names are logged as `<invalid>` (`577`), so an attacker cannot inject delimiters or newlines. Stored records are validated again on load (`377`, `467`).
- **Resource limits on hashing:** Passwords over 128 characters and empty passwords are rejected before hashing (`EmployeePortalAuth.java:347-349`). Iteration counts loaded from disk are capped at 5,000,000 (`381-383`), which stops a hash-cost denial of service.
- **Sensitive data in memory and logs:** Password arrays are wiped after use (`150`, `194-199`), `PBEKeySpec.clearPassword()` is called (`341`), and derived candidates are zeroed (`354`). The audit log records only event and username, never passwords (`576-578`). Error output shows only the I/O message, with no stack trace (`117`).
- **Password echo:** `Console.readPassword` is used when a terminal is present (`EmployeePortalAuth.java:662-664`). Without a console, the program prints an explicit warning that input will be visible (`677-680`). Accepted as documented behaviour.
- **File creation and temporary files (CWE-377, CWE-276):** New data files and temp files are created with `rw-------` (`614`, `626-629`). Temp files use unpredictable names from `Files.createTempFile` in the target directory and are atomically moved into place and cleaned up (`624-640`). Pre-existing directory and file permissions are not checked (SEC-03).
- **Not present / not applicable:** No SQL or NoSQL queries (no SQL injection), no object deserialization (`readAllLines` plus strict parsing only), no OS command execution, no XML parsing (no XXE), no outbound network or TLS use (no SSRF or transport issues), no JWT or session tokens, and no web output (no XSS).


---

### 35) results-cyber/claude/claude/set_a/sallie/6/basic/security_review.md

# Security Review: AdminPortal (Java command-line administrator portal)

## 1. Executive Summary
`AdminPortal.java` is a single-file Java 17 console program. It authenticates administrators against a local credential file (`admins.db`) and then offers an admin menu: list, add and remove administrators, change your own password, and view the audit log (`admin-audit.log`). Its core cryptography is sound. It uses PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 with 600,000 iterations and a 16-byte `SecureRandom` salt, compares hashes in constant time, runs a dummy hash for unknown users, shows one generic error message, and has no hard-coded credentials.

The weaknesses are in how the authentication is designed around that core:

- **SEC-01 (Medium):** whenever the credential store is empty or missing, anyone who runs the program can create an administrator without logging in. Both data files use paths relative to the working directory, so the store is easy to make empty.
- **SEC-02 (Medium):** the three-attempt limit only lives inside one process. Restarting the program, or running many copies at once, allows unlimited password guessing.
- **SEC-03 (Medium):** each session loads the credential file once and later overwrites the whole file, with no locking. An administrator who was removed keeps their session, and their next save can bring deleted accounts back.
- **Low findings:** there is no inactivity timeout or re-authentication before privileged actions. Hashing parameters read from the file are not validated. The audit log is created in a non-atomic way that follows symlinks, and no permission checks are made. When no terminal is available, passwords are echoed and held in immutable `String`s.

No injection, deserialization, command-execution or network issues exist because the program has none of those features.

## 2. Scope
| File | Purpose | Security-relevant behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| `AdminPortal.java` | The whole application: login loop, admin menu, credential store, audit log, file permission helper, console input | Password hashing (PBKDF2), salt/RNG, constant-time comparison, login attempt limiting, first-run admin bootstrap, account add/remove/password change, reading and writing `admins.db` (Java `Properties`, temp file plus atomic move), creating/appending/reading `admin-audit.log`, POSIX permission setting, password input with and without a console, clearing passwords from memory |
| `README.md` | Plain-English user documentation | Describes the security design and known limitations (per-run attempt limit, protecting `admins.db`, echoed passwords without a terminal). Used to confirm intended behaviour; not executable |
| `result.md`, `return.txt` | Metadata and summary from the generation run | No code; nothing security-relevant besides restating the design |
| `prompt.txt`, `cyber_prompt.txt` | Task prompts used to generate and review the code | No code |
| `prompt_hash.txt` | Empty file | None |

## 3. Skills Applied
- `review-code-for-security-vulnerabilities`: router workflow. Read and characterised every file, extracted keywords (password hashing, authentication, brute force, session, file permissions, race condition, audit log, sensitive data) and selected the specialised skills below.
- `performing-cryptographic-audit-of-application`: applied to PBKDF2 algorithm and parameters, salt generation, RNG, constant-time comparison, hard-coded secrets, and validation of KDF parameters read from `admins.db` (SEC-05).
- `testing-api-authentication-weaknesses`: its authentication checklist (missing authentication, brute-force/credential-stuffing resistance, password policy, account enumeration, session lifetime and revocation) applied to the console login, first-run bootstrap and admin session (SEC-01, SEC-02, SEC-04).
- `exploiting-race-condition-vulnerabilities`: its TOCTOU and limit-overrun concepts applied to the per-process attempt limit, concurrent sessions sharing `admins.db`, and check-then-create of the audit log (SEC-02, SEC-03, SEC-06).
- `testing-for-sensitive-data-exposure`: applied to insecure local storage of credential and audit files, error-message leakage, and passwords in memory and on screen (SEC-06, SEC-07).
- General OWASP Top 10 / CWE knowledge: used for local file-system concerns that no library skill covers (symlink following CWE-59, permissions CWE-732, relative data paths). Also used to confirm that no SQL, OS command, deserialization, XML, network/TLS or format-string surface exists.

## 4. Summary of Findings
| ID | Title | Severity | CWE | Location |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SEC-01 | Unauthenticated first-run admin creation whenever the credential store is empty or missing (cwd-relative paths) | Medium | CWE-306 | `AdminPortal.java:81` |
| SEC-02 | Login attempt limit is per process and resets on restart, so brute force is unlimited | Medium | CWE-307 | `AdminPortal.java:106` |
| SEC-03 | Unlocked, stale credential store: concurrent sessions overwrite each other; removed admins keep access and can restore accounts | Medium | CWE-362 | `AdminPortal.java:471` |

| SEC-07 | Without a console, passwords are echoed and kept in immutable Strings | Low | CWE-316 | `AdminPortal.java:529` |

## 5. Detailed Findings

### SEC-01: Unauthenticated first-run admin creation whenever the credential store is empty or missing (cwd-relative paths)
- **Severity:** Medium
- **CWE:** CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function
- **Location:** `AdminPortal.java:44-45`, `AdminPortal.java:81-89`, `AdminPortal.java:445`

**Vulnerable code:**
```java
// AdminPortal.java:44-45
    private static final Path CREDENTIALS_FILE = Paths.get("admins.db");
    private static final Path AUDIT_LOG = Paths.get("admin-audit.log");
// AdminPortal.java:81-89
        if (store.isEmpty()) {
            System.out.println("No administrator accounts exist yet. Let's create the first one.");
            String created = createAdmin();
            if (created == null) {
                System.out.println("Setup cancelled. Exiting.");
                return;
            }
            audit("SETUP", created, "initial administrator created");
        }
```

**Why it is a problem:** Creating an administrator is the most privileged action in the program, yet it needs no authentication whenever `CredentialStore.load` finds no file (`Files.exists(file)` at line 445) or an empty one. The program then goes straight to the login it has just set up for the caller, and the caller receives "Access granted".

Both data paths are relative to the working directory, so this state is easy to reach:
- Running `java AdminPortal` from any other directory produces a fresh, empty store.
- Anyone with write access to the directory can delete or rename `admins.db`. The file's 0600 mode does not stop this, because deleting a file needs only directory write permission. The next run then lets that person become the "first" administrator.

The program never distinguishes an intentional first install from a missing, moved or tampered credential file. It fails open instead of refusing to start.

**Fix:** Keep the data in a fixed, absolute, owner-only directory. Make bootstrap an explicit, separate action (an `--init` flag run by the service owner) that only works when the file does not exist yet. At every normal start, a missing or empty store must be a fatal error.
```java
private static final Path DATA_DIR =
        Paths.get(System.getProperty("adminportal.dir", "/var/lib/adminportal")).toAbsolutePath();
private static final Path CREDENTIALS_FILE = DATA_DIR.resolve("admins.db");
private static final Path AUDIT_LOG = DATA_DIR.resolve("admin-audit.log");

public static void main(String[] args) {
    boolean init = args.length == 1 && args[0].equals("--init");
    try {
        FileSecurity.verifyPrivateDirectory(DATA_DIR); // owned by current user, not group/other writable
        if (!init && !Files.exists(CREDENTIALS_FILE, LinkOption.NOFOLLOW_LINKS)) {
            System.err.println("Credential store " + CREDENTIALS_FILE + " is missing. Refusing to start.");
            System.exit(1);
        }
        AdminPortal portal = new AdminPortal(CredentialStore.load(CREDENTIALS_FILE), new Input());
        portal.run(init);
    } catch (IOException e) {
        System.err.println("Error: could not access portal data files (" + e.getMessage() + ").");
        System.exit(1);
    }
}

private void run(boolean init) throws IOException {
    System.out.println("=== Administrator Portal ===");
    if (store.isEmpty()) {
        if (!init) {
            audit("SETUP_REFUSED", "<none>", "credential store empty");
            System.err.println("No administrator accounts exist. Run 'java AdminPortal --init' as the service owner.");
            return;
        }
        String created = createAdmin();
        if (created == null) {
            System.out.println("Setup cancelled. Exiting.");
            return;
        }
        audit("SETUP", created, "initial administrator created");
    } else if (init) {
        System.err.println("--init refused: administrator accounts already exist.");
        return;
    }
    // ... login() and adminMenu() as before
}
```

### SEC-02: Login attempt limit is per process and resets on restart, so brute force is unlimited
- **Severity:** Medium
- **CWE:** CWE-307: Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts
- **Location:** `AdminPortal.java:52-53`, `AdminPortal.java:106-138` (also `AdminPortal.java:274-278` for current-password re-checks)

**Vulnerable code:**
```java
// AdminPortal.java:106-138
        for (int attempt = 1; attempt <= MAX_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS; attempt++) {
            System.out.println();
            String username = input.readLine("Username: ");
            if (username == null) {
                return null; // end of input
            }
            username = username.trim();

            char[] password = input.readPassword("Password: ");
            if (password == null) {
                return null;
            }

            boolean ok;
            try {
                ok = authenticate(username, password);
            } finally {
                Arrays.fill(password, '\0');
            }

            String logName = USERNAME_PATTERN.matcher(username).matches() ? username : "<invalid>";
            if (ok) {
                audit("LOGIN_SUCCESS", logName, "");
                return username;
            }

            audit("LOGIN_FAILURE", logName, "attempt " + attempt);
            // Same message whether the username or the password was wrong.
            System.out.println("Invalid username or password.");
            sleepQuietly(FAILURE_DELAY_MS * attempt);
        }
        System.out.println("Too many failed attempts.");
        return null;
```

**Why it is a problem:** The attempt counter and growing delay live only in the local variable `attempt`. Nothing is stored between runs, so the limit does not survive a restart. An attacker who can run the program can script it through stdin; the non-console path at lines 508-518 accepts piped input. Starting a new process for each guess, or running many in parallel, skips the 2 s/4 s delays entirely. The only brake left is PBKDF2 cost (roughly 0.3-1 s per guess per core), which still allows thousands of guesses per hour against an admin account. The failures are logged but never acted on.

The same issue appears inside a session: `changePassword` re-checks the current password with only a 2 s delay and no limit. Someone at an unattended logged-in terminal can therefore guess the password without limit. This is the limit-overrun pattern from the race-condition skill, where a rate limit held in volatile per-request state can be bypassed by making many independent attempts.

**Fix:** Keep a failure counter per account (plus one bucket for invalid names) in a locked, owner-only file. Check it before hashing and apply an escalating lockout. Use the same check for the current-password prompt in `changePassword`.
```java
/** Failed-login counters that survive restarts and are shared by concurrent processes. */
static final class LoginThrottle {
    private static final Path FILE = DATA_DIR.resolve("login-throttle.db");
    private static final int MAX_FAILURES = 5;
    private static final long LOCKOUT_MS = 15 * 60 * 1000L;

    private interface Update { void apply(Properties p); }

    private static Properties update(Update u) throws IOException {
        try (FileChannel ch = FileChannel.open(FILE,
                     Set.of(StandardOpenOption.CREATE, StandardOpenOption.READ,
                            StandardOpenOption.WRITE, LinkOption.NOFOLLOW_LINKS),
                     PosixFilePermissions.asFileAttribute(PosixFilePermissions.fromString("rw-------")));
             FileLock lock = ch.lock()) {
            Properties p = new Properties();
            p.load(Channels.newInputStream(ch));
            u.apply(p);
            ch.truncate(0);
            ch.position(0);
            p.store(Channels.newOutputStream(ch), null);
            return p;
        }
    }

    static boolean isLocked(String key) throws IOException {
        long until = Long.parseLong(update(p -> { }).getProperty(key + ".until", "0"));
        return System.currentTimeMillis() < until;
    }

    static void recordFailure(String key) throws IOException {
        update(p -> {
            int n = Integer.parseInt(p.getProperty(key + ".failures", "0")) + 1;
            p.setProperty(key + ".failures", Integer.toString(n));
            if (n >= MAX_FAILURES) {
                long backoff = LOCKOUT_MS << Math.min(n - MAX_FAILURES, 6);
                p.setProperty(key + ".until", Long.toString(System.currentTimeMillis() + backoff));
            }
        });
    }

    static void reset(String key) throws IOException {
        update(p -> { p.remove(key + ".failures"); p.remove(key + ".until"); });
    }
}

// in login(), before authenticate():
String logName = USERNAME_PATTERN.matcher(username).matches() ? username : "<invalid>";
if (LoginThrottle.isLocked(logName)) {
    Arrays.fill(password, '\0');
    audit("LOGIN_LOCKED", logName, "attempt " + attempt);
    System.out.println("Invalid username or password.");
    sleepQuietly(FAILURE_DELAY_MS * attempt);
    continue;
}
boolean ok;
try {
    ok = authenticate(username, password);
} finally {
    Arrays.fill(password, '\0');
}
if (ok) {
    LoginThrottle.reset(logName);
    audit("LOGIN_SUCCESS", logName, "");
    return username;
}
LoginThrottle.recordFailure(logName);
```

### SEC-03: Unlocked, stale credential store: concurrent sessions overwrite each other; removed admins keep access and can restore accounts
- **Severity:** Medium
- **CWE:** CWE-362: Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization ('Race Condition')
- **Location:** `AdminPortal.java:70`, `AdminPortal.java:257-258`, `AdminPortal.java:286-287`, `AdminPortal.java:471-486`

**Vulnerable code:**
```java
// AdminPortal.java:471-486
        void save() throws IOException {
            Properties props = new Properties();
            entries.forEach((name, hash) -> props.setProperty(name, hash.encode()));

            Path dir = file.toAbsolutePath().getParent();
            Path tmp = Files.createTempFile(dir, "admins", ".tmp");
            try {
                FileSecurity.restrictToOwner(tmp);
                try (Writer w = Files.newBufferedWriter(tmp, StandardCharsets.UTF_8)) {
                    props.store(w, "Administrator credentials (PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256: iterations:salt:hash)");
                }
                Files.move(tmp, file, StandardCopyOption.REPLACE_EXISTING, StandardCopyOption.ATOMIC_MOVE);
            } finally {
                Files.deleteIfExists(tmp);
            }
        }
```

**Why it is a problem:** `admins.db` is read only once, at start-up (line 70). Every later `save()` writes that process's in-memory map over the whole file, with no file lock and no re-read. When two administrators are logged in at the same time (two processes):

1. Admin A removes admin B, for example because B's password was leaked (lines 257-258). The file no longer lists B.
2. B's session is not checked again. B stays in the menu and keeps full admin rights; nothing ever checks `store.get(currentUser)` again.
3. B chooses "Change my password" or "Add administrator". B's stale map still contains B, and `save()` replaces the file, so B is restored. Any accounts A added or removed in the meantime are silently undone.

This defeats account revocation. It also loses updates between honest administrators, so audit log entries such as "removed X" no longer match the real state of the file.

**Fix:** Serialise every change with an exclusive lock. Under the lock, re-read the file, apply the change and save. Before each menu action, check that the current user still exists, and end the session if it does not.
```java
// CredentialStore
void reload() throws IOException {
    CredentialStore fresh = load(file);
    entries.clear();
    entries.putAll(fresh.entries);
}

/** Re-reads the file under an exclusive lock, applies the change, and saves before releasing the lock. */
void modify(java.util.function.Consumer<CredentialStore> change) throws IOException {
    Path lockFile = file.resolveSibling(file.getFileName() + ".lock");
    try (FileChannel ch = FileChannel.open(lockFile, StandardOpenOption.CREATE, StandardOpenOption.WRITE);
         FileLock lock = ch.lock()) {
        reload();
        change.accept(this);
        save();
    }
}

// adminMenu(): at the top of every loop iteration
store.reload();
if (store.get(currentUser) == null) {
    audit("SESSION_REVOKED", currentUser, "account no longer exists");
    System.out.println("Your administrator account has been removed. Logging out.");
    return;
}

// changePassword(): replace store.put(...) / store.save()
StoredHash newHash = StoredHash.create(password);
store.modify(s -> {
    if (s.get(currentUser) == null) {
        throw new IllegalStateException("account was removed");
    }
    s.put(currentUser, newHash);
});

// removeAdmin(): replace store.remove(...) / store.save()
store.modify(s -> s.remove(username));
```

### SEC-04: No idle timeout on admin session and no re-authentication before adding or removing administrators
- **Severity:** Low
- **CWE:** CWE-613: Insufficient Session Expiration
- **Location:** `AdminPortal.java:155-198`

**Vulnerable code:**
```java
// AdminPortal.java:166-184
            String choice = input.readLine("Choose an option: ");
            if (choice == null) {
                choice = "6";
            }

            switch (choice.trim()) {
                case "1":
                    listAdmins();
                    break;
                case "2": {
                    String created = createAdmin();
                    if (created != null) {
                        audit("ADMIN_ADDED", currentUser, "added " + created);
                    }
                    break;
                }
                case "3":
                    removeAdmin(currentUser);
                    break;
```

**Why it is a problem:** After one successful login the menu loop runs forever. The session has no inactivity or absolute timeout. Creating a new administrator (a persistent backdoor account) and removing other administrators require no fresh proof of identity, even though changing your own password does. Anyone who reaches an unattended terminal where an admin is logged in (or a stale `tmux`/`screen` session) can add their own admin account or lock out the real administrators. The authentication-weaknesses skill flags this under session lifetime and revocation.

**Fix:** Track the time since the last activity and end the session once it passes an idle limit. Ask for the current password again before privileged account changes.
```java
private static final Duration IDLE_TIMEOUT = Duration.ofMinutes(5);

private void adminMenu(String currentUser) throws IOException {
    Instant lastActivity = Instant.now();
    while (true) {
        // ... print menu ...
        String choice = input.readLine("Choose an option: ");
        if (Duration.between(lastActivity, Instant.now()).compareTo(IDLE_TIMEOUT) > 0) {
            audit("SESSION_TIMEOUT", currentUser, "");
            System.out.println("Session expired due to inactivity. Please log in again.");
            return;
        }
        lastActivity = Instant.now();
        if (choice == null) {
            choice = "6";
        }
        switch (choice.trim()) {
            case "2": {
                if (!reauthenticate(currentUser)) {
                    break;
                }
                String created = createAdmin();
                if (created != null) {
                    audit("ADMIN_ADDED", currentUser, "added " + created);
                }
                break;
            }
            case "3":
                if (reauthenticate(currentUser)) {
                    removeAdmin(currentUser);
                }
                break;
            // ... other cases unchanged ...
        }
    }
}

private boolean reauthenticate(String currentUser) throws IOException {
    char[] pw = input.readPassword("Re-enter your password: ");
    if (pw == null) {
        return false;
    }
    try {
        if (authenticate(currentUser, pw)) {
            return true;
        }
    } finally {
        Arrays.fill(pw, '\0');
    }
    audit("REAUTH_FAILURE", currentUser, "");
    System.out.println("Password incorrect.");
    sleepQuietly(FAILURE_DELAY_MS);
    return false;
}
```

### SEC-05: KDF parameters (iteration count, salt and hash length) from `admins.db` not validated
- **Severity:** Low
- **CWE:** CWE-1284: Improper Validation of Specified Quantity in Input
- **Location:** `AdminPortal.java:418-425` (used at `AdminPortal.java:146`)

**Vulnerable code:**
```java
// AdminPortal.java:418-425
        static StoredHash decode(String value) {
            String[] parts = value.split(":");
            if (parts.length != 3) {
                throw new IllegalArgumentException("malformed entry");
            }
            Base64.Decoder b64 = Base64.getDecoder();
            return new StoredHash(Integer.parseInt(parts[0]), b64.decode(parts[1]), b64.decode(parts[2]));
        }
```

**Why it is a problem:** The iteration count, salt and hash come straight from the file and are trusted without checks. The crypto-audit skill's "weak KDF parameters" check applies here:
- **Downgrade:** `iterations` can be `1`, and `CredentialStore.load` accepts it. That makes an entry trivial to crack offline and hides the tampering from the load-time integrity check.
- **Crash:** `0`, a negative value or an empty salt passes `load` but makes `new PBEKeySpec(...)` throw an uncaught `IllegalArgumentException` inside `authenticate` (line 146). The program then crashes at login for that user, a denial of service.
- **Hang:** a very large value such as `2147483647` makes login appear to hang indefinitely.
- **Hash length:** hash length is never checked either.

Changing these values requires write access to the file, so the impact is limited. Still, input parsing should reject values outside a safe policy rather than fail late or weaken the hash without notice.

**Fix:** Validate the parameters in `decode` so a bad entry is reported as corruption at load time.
```java
private static final int MIN_ITERATIONS = 600_000;
private static final int MAX_ITERATIONS = 10_000_000;

static StoredHash decode(String value) {
    String[] parts = value.split(":");
    if (parts.length != 3) {
        throw new IllegalArgumentException("malformed entry");
    }
    int iterations = Integer.parseInt(parts[0]);
    if (iterations < MIN_ITERATIONS || iterations > MAX_ITERATIONS) {
        throw new IllegalArgumentException("unacceptable iteration count");
    }
    Base64.Decoder b64 = Base64.getDecoder();
    byte[] salt = b64.decode(parts[1]);
    byte[] hash = b64.decode(parts[2]);
    if (salt.length < SALT_BYTES || hash.length != HASH_BITS / 8) {
        throw new IllegalArgumentException("unacceptable salt or hash length");
    }
    return new StoredHash(iterations, salt, hash);
}
```

### SEC-06: Audit log created with default permissions and then chmod-ed, follows symlinks, and data-file permissions never checked
- **Severity:** Low
- **CWE:** CWE-732: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
- **Location:** `AdminPortal.java:374-377`, `AdminPortal.java:491-494`, `AdminPortal.java:445-449`

**Vulnerable code:**
```java
// AdminPortal.java:374-377
            if (!Files.exists(AUDIT_LOG)) {
                FileSecurity.createPrivateFile(AUDIT_LOG);
            }
            Files.writeString(AUDIT_LOG, line, StandardCharsets.UTF_8, StandardOpenOption.APPEND);
// AdminPortal.java:491-494
        static void createPrivateFile(Path path) throws IOException {
            Files.createFile(path);
            restrictToOwner(path);
        }
```

**Why it is a problem:**
- **Brief permission window:** `Files.createFile` applies the process umask (usually 0644), and 0600 is only set afterwards. For that short window another local user can open the log for reading and keep the handle.
- **Check-then-create race (CWE-367):** the existence check and the creation are separate steps. If the file appears between them, `createFile` fails and the audit event is silently lost. On a failure, the program only prints a warning and continues.
- **Symlink following (CWE-59):** `Files.writeString(..., APPEND)` follows symlinks. If `admin-audit.log` is a link planted in a shared working directory (see SEC-01), the log is appended to whatever file the link points at. If the log already exists with loose permissions or belongs to someone else, it is used as is.
- **Credential file not checked:** `CredentialStore.load` (lines 445-449) reads `admins.db` without checking its owner or mode. A group- or world-writable credential file is trusted, even though anyone who can edit it can add an administrator.

**Fix:** Create and open the file in one atomic step with owner-only permissions and `NOFOLLOW_LINKS`, and don't use a separate `exists` check. Before trusting either data file, confirm it is a regular file owned by the current user and not accessible to group or others.
```java
private static final Set<PosixFilePermission> OWNER_RW = PosixFilePermissions.fromString("rw-------");

private static void audit(String event, String username, String detail) {
    String line = Instant.now() + " " + event + " user=" + username
            + (detail.isEmpty() ? "" : " " + detail) + System.lineSeparator();
    Set<OpenOption> opts = Set.of(StandardOpenOption.CREATE, StandardOpenOption.APPEND,
            StandardOpenOption.WRITE, LinkOption.NOFOLLOW_LINKS);
    try (SeekableByteChannel ch = Files.newByteChannel(AUDIT_LOG, opts,
            PosixFilePermissions.asFileAttribute(OWNER_RW))) {
        FileSecurity.verifyPrivate(AUDIT_LOG);
        ch.write(ByteBuffer.wrap(line.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8)));
    } catch (IOException e) {
        System.err.println("Warning: could not write audit log: " + e.getMessage());
    }
}

// FileSecurity
static void verifyPrivate(Path path) throws IOException {
    PosixFileAttributes a = Files.readAttributes(path, PosixFileAttributes.class, LinkOption.NOFOLLOW_LINKS);
    String me = System.getProperty("user.name");
    boolean shared = a.permissions().stream()
            .anyMatch(p -> p.name().startsWith("GROUP_") || p.name().startsWith("OTHERS_"));
    if (!a.isRegularFile() || !a.owner().getName().equals(me) || shared) {
        throw new IOException(path + " must be a regular file owned by " + me + " with mode 0600");
    }
}

// CredentialStore.load(): before reading
if (Files.exists(file, LinkOption.NOFOLLOW_LINKS)) {
    FileSecurity.verifyPrivate(file);
    // ... load as before ...
}
```

### SEC-07: Without a console, passwords are echoed and kept in immutable Strings
- **Severity:** Low
- **CWE:** CWE-316: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information in Memory
- **Location:** `AdminPortal.java:521-531`

**Vulnerable code:**
```java
// AdminPortal.java:521-531
        char[] readPassword(String prompt) throws IOException {
            if (console != null) {
                return console.readPassword("%s", prompt);
            }
            if (!warned) {
                System.err.println("Warning: no terminal detected; password input will not be hidden.");
                warned = true;
            }
            String line = readLine(prompt);
            return line == null ? null : line.toCharArray();
        }
```

**Why it is a problem:** When `System.console()` is null (IDE runs, piped or redirected stdin, some `ssh`/`sudo`/container setups), the program still accepts passwords. They are shown on screen and may end up in terminal scrollback or session recordings; this also falls under CWE-549, missing password field masking. Each password is also read into a `String` (line 529), which is immutable and cannot be wiped. Every login, new-password, confirm-password and current-password entry therefore stays in the heap until garbage collection, and can be exposed through heap dumps, core files or swap. That undermines the promise at line 40 and in the README that passwords are "wiped from memory after use". A warning does not stop the insecure path.

**Fix:** By default, refuse to read passwords without a console. If non-interactive use is really needed, allow it only through an explicit opt-in, and read straight into a `char[]` that is cleared afterwards.
```java
char[] readPassword(String prompt) throws IOException {
    if (console != null) {
        return console.readPassword("%s", prompt);
    }
    if (!Boolean.getBoolean("adminportal.allowNonInteractive")) {
        throw new IOException("refusing to read a password without a terminal (input would be echoed)");
    }
    System.out.print(prompt);
    System.out.flush();
    char[] buf = new char[MAX_PASSWORD_LENGTH + 1];
    int n = 0;
    int c;
    while ((c = reader.read()) != -1 && c != '\n') {
        if (c == '\r') {
            continue;
        }
        if (n == buf.length) {
            Arrays.fill(buf, '\0');
            throw new IOException("password too long");
        }
        buf[n++] = (char) c;
    }
    if (c == -1 && n == 0) {
        return null;
    }
    char[] result = Arrays.copyOf(buf, n);
    Arrays.fill(buf, '\0');
    return result;
}
```

## 6. Verified Controls and Checks With No Finding
- **Password hashing algorithm and parameters:** PBKDF2WithHmacSHA256, 600,000 iterations, 256-bit output (`AdminPortal.java:47-50`, `358-367`). This meets current OWASP guidance for newly created hashes. No MD5, SHA-1 or unsalted hashing anywhere.
- **Salt and RNG:** a 16-byte salt is generated for every password from a single `SecureRandom` (`AdminPortal.java:49`, `58`, `408-411`, `427-431`). No `java.util.Random` or time-based seeds.
- **Hard-coded or default credentials:** none. No passwords, keys or default accounts in source or README (`AdminPortal.java:33-34`, `81-89`). The bootstrap weakness is covered separately in SEC-01.
- **Constant-time comparison and user enumeration:** `MessageDigest.isEqual` compares hashes (`AdminPortal.java:147`). Unknown or invalid usernames still run a full PBKDF2 against `StoredHash.DUMMY`, which uses the same iteration count (`AdminPortal.java:143-146`, `396`). The same "Invalid username or password." message is shown in every failure case (`AdminPortal.java:134`).
- **Password policy:** 12-128 characters, with upper case, lower case, a digit and a symbol, enforced on creation and on change (`AdminPortal.java:309-354`). The 128-character maximum bounds hashing cost. New passwords are entered twice (`AdminPortal.java:322`).
- **Password clearing on the console path:** password arrays are zeroed in `finally` blocks (`AdminPortal.java:122-124`, `231-233`, `271-273`, `288-290`, `334-336`). `PBEKeySpec.clearPassword()` is called (`AdminPortal.java:365`) and the computed hash is zeroed (`AdminPortal.java:148`). The non-console path is covered in SEC-07.
- **Log and terminal injection:** usernames are restricted to `^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{3,32}$` when created (`AdminPortal.java:215`), when loaded (`AdminPortal.java:452`) and before an attempted username is logged (`AdminPortal.java:126`). Log details are fixed strings or validated names, so no CR/LF or ANSI escape can reach `admin-audit.log` or the screen through `showAuditLog` (`AdminPortal.java:295-306`). Passwords are never logged.
- **Format strings:** `Console.readLine` and `readPassword` use the constant `"%s"` format with the prompt as an argument (`AdminPortal.java:514`, `523`), so there is no format-string injection.
- **Credential file writes:** a temp file created by `Files.createTempFile` (0600 on POSIX) is atomically moved over `admins.db`, so partial writes cannot happen and the replaced file is not accessed through a symlink (`AdminPortal.java:475-485`). Concurrency and permission checks are covered in SEC-03 and SEC-06.
- **Credential file parsing:** `java.util.Properties` text parsing only, with no object deserialization. Malformed Base64 and number parsing errors are caught and reported as corruption (`AdminPortal.java:446-458`). Parameter ranges are covered in SEC-05.
- **Self-lockout and destructive actions:** an admin cannot remove their own account, and removal requires typing the name twice (`AdminPortal.java:244-256`). Password change requires the current password (`AdminPortal.java:264-279`).
- **Error handling and information leakage:** errors go only to the local stderr and include file I/O messages (`AdminPortal.java:73`, `379`). No stack traces are shown, and no credential material appears in any message. This is acceptable for a local admin tool.
- **Injection and other attack surface:** no SQL or JDBC, no `Runtime.exec`/`ProcessBuilder`, no reflection, no `ObjectInputStream`, no XML parsing, no network sockets, HTTP or TLS, and no user-controlled file paths. OWASP A03 (injection), A08 (deserialization) and A10 (SSRF) do not apply.
- **Non-code files:** `README.md`, `result.md`, `return.txt`, `prompt.txt`, `cyber_prompt.txt` and `prompt_hash.txt` were reviewed. None contains executable code, secrets or credentials.


---

### 36) results-cyber/claude/claude/set_a/sallie/6/security/security_review.md

# Security Review: AdminPortal (Java command-line administrator portal)

## 1. Executive Summary
`AdminPortal.java` is a single-file Java 17 command-line program. It authenticates administrators with a username and password, then opens a small admin menu: list admins, create an admin, view audit events, verify the audit log, log out. It stores PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 password hashes in `admins.db`, keeps failed-login counts in `lockouts.properties`, and writes every authentication event to `audit.log`, a SHA-256 hash-chained file.

The code is careful overall. Password hashing is strong, the hash comparison is constant-time, login errors are generic, unknown usernames are timing-equalised, log fields are escaped against injection, and the program fails closed when audit writes fail. No Critical or High issues were found. The most important findings are:

- **SEC-01 (Medium):** Lockout state is read, checked and rewritten with no lock between processes. Running many `login` processes in parallel lets an attacker go past the 5-failure limit and can even erase an active lock.
- **SEC-02 (Medium):** The data directory defaults to a path relative to the working directory. An existing directory is trusted without checking its owner, permissions or symlinks. Anyone who can write there can plant their own `admins.db` and get admin access, or rewrite the audit log.
- **SEC-03 (Medium):** `setup` checks "no administrators exist" only before its interactive prompts. The final write only rejects duplicate usernames, so a second unauthenticated "first administrator" can be created.
- Six Low findings:
  - Passwords typed into the username field are logged and shown to every admin.
  - The idle timeout is not enforced during admin creation.
  - Passwords are echoed when no `Console` is attached.
  - The audit hash chain is unkeyed and not anchored anywhere else, so deleting the newest entries goes undetected.
  - The password policy has no common-password blocklist.
  - Error messages include internal file paths.

## 2. Scope
| File | Purpose | Security-relevant behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| `AdminPortal.java` | The whole application: CLI entry point, `Portal` workflows (setup/login/admin menu), `Authenticator`, `Validation`, `PasswordHasher`, `CredentialStore`, `LockoutTracker`, `AuditLog`, `FileUtil`, `Terminal` | Password authentication, PBKDF2 hashing with salt, constant-time compare, account lockout and brute-force throttling, user-enumeration defences, session idle timeout, admin creation, hash-chained audit logging and log-injection escaping, file and directory permissions, atomic writes, cross-process file locking, console password input, error handling |
| `README.md` | User documentation for the program | Documents the intended controls and known limits (hash chain only detects changes, data-folder trust, usernames logged, password hiding needs a terminal). Used to check that the code matches its stated security properties. |
| `result.md` | Run metadata and summary from the session that generated the code | No executable code. Restates the claimed controls and limits. |
| `prompt.txt` | Original requirement for the program | No executable code. Requires authentication plus logging of every success and failure. |
| `cyber_prompt.txt` | Instructions for this security review | No executable code. |
| `return.txt` | JSON result record of the generating session | No executable code, no secrets affecting the application. |
| `prompt_hash.txt` | Empty file | None. |

## 3. Skills Applied
- `review-code-for-security-vulnerabilities`: The router workflow. Understood every file, searched the skill library by name for the behaviours found, and applied the matches below in priority order.
- `testing-api-authentication-weaknesses`: Applied to the login flow in `Authenticator.authenticate`:
  - Account-enumeration resistance (generic message, dummy hashing)
  - Brute-force and lockout controls
  - Password policy (`Validation.passwordProblem`)
  - Session lifecycle (idle timeout in `adminSession`)
  - Credential leakage into logs

  The JWT, refresh-token and HTTP-endpoint checks do not apply to this CLI and were skipped.
- `exploiting-race-condition-vulnerabilities`: Applied its TOCTOU and limit-overrun methodology to two places. The first is the attempt-limiting logic (`LockoutTracker` plus `Authenticator`) when many processes run at once. The second is the multi-step `setup` workflow and `CredentialStore.add`.
- `performing-cryptographic-audit-of-application`: Applied to `PasswordHasher`:
  - Algorithm, iteration count, salt size and source, output length

  - Iteration count and salt read back from `admins.db`

- `implementing-log-integrity-with-blockchain`: Applied to the `AuditLog` hash chain: genesis value, chain construction, verification, tamper detection, and external checkpoint anchoring.
- `testing-for-sensitive-data-exposure`: Applied to secrets in logs (`audit.record` of raw usernames, audit tail shown to admins), information leakage in error messages (`main`, `CredentialStore.load`), and protection of data at rest (file and directory permissions).
- General OWASP Top 10 / CWE review, because no library skill matched these behaviours:

  - Terminal password masking (CWE-549)

## 5. Detailed Findings

### SEC-01: Account lockout can be bypassed by running `login` processes in parallel
- **Severity:** Medium
- **CWE:** CWE-362: Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization ('Race Condition'). Also CWE-307: Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts.
- **Location:** `AdminPortal.java:318-331`, `AdminPortal.java:523-541`

**Vulnerable code:**
```java
// AdminPortal.java:318-331
            Optional<Instant> lockedUntil = lockouts.lockedUntil(username, now);
            if (lockedUntil.isPresent()) {
                PasswordHasher.burnEquivalentTime(password);
                audit.record("LOGIN_FAILURE", username, "FAILURE", "account locked until " + lockedUntil.get());
                return Optional.empty();
            }

            if (PasswordHasher.matches(password, stored)) {
                audit.record("LOGIN_SUCCESS", username, "SUCCESS", "access granted");
                lockouts.recordSuccess(username);
                return Optional.of(username);
            }

            boolean nowLocked = lockouts.recordFailure(username, now);
// AdminPortal.java:523-541
        synchronized boolean recordFailure(String username, Instant now) throws IOException {
            Properties props = load();
            long nowSeconds = now.getEpochSecond();
            long[] state = state(props, username); // [failures, windowStart, lockedUntil]
            boolean windowExpired = nowSeconds - state[1] > FAILURE_WINDOW.getSeconds();
            boolean lockExpired = state[2] != 0 && nowSeconds >= state[2];
            if (windowExpired || lockExpired) {
                state = new long[] {0, nowSeconds, 0};
            }
            state[0]++;
            boolean locked = false;
            if (state[0] >= MAX_FAILURES) {
                state[2] = nowSeconds + LOCK_DURATION.getSeconds();
                locked = true;
            }
            props.setProperty(username, state[0] + "," + state[1] + "," + state[2]);
            save(props);
            return locked;
        }
```

**Why it is a problem:** Each `java AdminPortal.java login` is a separate JVM. `synchronized` only serialises threads inside one process, and `LockoutTracker` takes no file lock, unlike `AuditLog.record`. The lock check (line 318) and the failure update (line 331) are separated by a deliberately slow PBKDF2 computation of 600,000 iterations. The update is a load, modify, rewrite of the whole file.

An attacker who can start the program many times at once (for example through a sudo rule or an SSH forced command) can do three things:
1. All N processes pass the "not locked" check before any of them records a failure. Each process allows 3 attempts per run (`MAX_ATTEMPTS_PER_RUN`), so N processes get far more than 5 guesses per 15-minute window.
2. Concurrent load/rewrite cycles lose increments, because the last writer wins, so the counter under-counts.
3. A process that loaded the file before the lock was written can later write back `failures=4, lockedUntil=0` and silently remove an active lock.

The fixed per-account window also has no global limit, so password spraying across several admin accounts is not throttled. The lockout is the only real brute-force control; the 3-attempt limit per run is reset simply by starting the program again.

**Fix:** Serialise lockout state across processes with an OS file lock. Use a separate, stable lock file, because `writeAtomically` replaces `lockouts.properties` and a lock on the replaced file would mean nothing. Reserve (count) the attempt before the expensive hash check, so parallel attempts cannot all pass the check. Clear the count only on success. Consider also adding a global failure budget across all accounts.
```java
// LockoutTracker: constructed with dataDir.resolve("lockouts.properties") and dataDir.resolve("lockouts.lock")
private final Path file;
private final Path lockFile;

/**
 * Atomically counts one attempt BEFORE the password is checked.
 * Returns the lock expiry if the account is already locked (the attempt is then refused).
 */
Optional<Instant> reserveAttempt(String username, Instant now) throws IOException {
    FileUtil.createPrivateFileIfMissing(lockFile);
    try (FileChannel channel = FileChannel.open(lockFile, StandardOpenOption.WRITE);
         FileLock lock = channel.lock()) { // cross-process mutual exclusion
        Properties props = load();
        long nowSeconds = now.getEpochSecond();
        long[] state = state(props, username);
        if (state[2] != 0 && nowSeconds < state[2]) {
            return Optional.of(Instant.ofEpochSecond(state[2]));
        }
        if (nowSeconds - state[1] > FAILURE_WINDOW.getSeconds() || state[2] != 0) {
            state = new long[] {0, nowSeconds, 0};
        }
        state[0]++;
        if (state[0] >= MAX_FAILURES) {
            state[2] = nowSeconds + LOCK_DURATION.getSeconds(); // later concurrent attempts are refused
        }
        props.setProperty(username, state[0] + "," + state[1] + "," + state[2]);
        save(props);
        return Optional.empty();
    }
}

void recordSuccess(String username) throws IOException {
    FileUtil.createPrivateFileIfMissing(lockFile);
    try (FileChannel channel = FileChannel.open(lockFile, StandardOpenOption.WRITE);
         FileLock lock = channel.lock()) {
        Properties props = load();
        if (props.remove(username) != null) {
            save(props);
        }
    }
}

// Authenticator.authenticate
Optional<Instant> lockedUntil = lockouts.reserveAttempt(username, now);
if (lockedUntil.isPresent()) {
    PasswordHasher.burnEquivalentTime(password);
    audit.record("LOGIN_FAILURE", username, "FAILURE", "account locked until " + lockedUntil.get());
    return Optional.empty();
}
if (PasswordHasher.matches(password, stored)) {
    audit.record("LOGIN_SUCCESS", username, "SUCCESS", "access granted");
    lockouts.recordSuccess(username);
    return Optional.of(username);
}
audit.record("LOGIN_FAILURE", username, "FAILURE", "incorrect password"); // failure was already counted
return Optional.empty();
```

### SEC-02: Data directory trusted without ownership, permission or symlink checks, and resolved relative to the working directory
- **Severity:** Medium
- **CWE:** CWE-732: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource. Related: CWE-59 Improper Link Resolution Before File Access, CWE-427 Uncontrolled Search Path Element.
- **Location:** `AdminPortal.java:90-103`, `AdminPortal.java:616-617`

**Vulnerable code:**
```java
// AdminPortal.java:90-103
    private static Path resolveDataDir() throws IOException {
        String configured = System.getenv("ADMIN_PORTAL_HOME");
        Path dir = Paths.get(configured == null || configured.isBlank() ? "admin-portal-data" : configured)
                .toAbsolutePath().normalize();
        if (!Files.exists(dir)) {
            try {
                Files.createDirectories(dir, PosixFilePermissions.asFileAttribute(
                        PosixFilePermissions.fromString("rwx------")));
            } catch (UnsupportedOperationException e) {
                Files.createDirectories(dir); // Non-POSIX file system (e.g. Windows)
            }
        }
        return dir;
    }
// AdminPortal.java:616-617
            FileUtil.createPrivateFileIfMissing(file);
            try (FileChannel channel = FileChannel.open(file, StandardOpenOption.READ, StandardOpenOption.WRITE);
```

**Why it is a problem:** All authentication decisions come from files in this directory: `admins.db` defines who is an administrator, `lockouts.properties` defines who is locked, and `audit.log` is the evidence trail. The owner-only permissions are applied only when the program creates the directory. If the directory already exists, whatever permissions, owner or symlink it has are silently accepted.

With `ADMIN_PORTAL_HOME` unset, the path is relative to the current working directory. An administrator who runs the tool from a shared or attacker-writable directory (for example `/tmp` or a shared project folder) uses an `admin-portal-data` directory that someone else may have pre-created. That attacker can:
- Plant an `admins.db` containing their own PBKDF2 hash and log in as an administrator.
- Delete or replace `lockouts.properties` to reset lockouts.
- Rewrite `audit.log` and recompute the unkeyed chain (see SEC-07).
- Point `audit.log` at another file through a symlink. `FileChannel.open` follows symlinks, so the victim's process appends to whatever file the link targets.

On Windows the fallback at line 99 creates the directory with inherited ACLs and no restriction at all.

**Fix:** Require an explicit absolute data directory. Refuse to start unless it is a real directory (not a symlink), owned by the running account, and has no group or other permissions. Open data files with `LinkOption.NOFOLLOW_LINKS`.
```java
private static Path resolveDataDir() throws IOException {
    String configured = System.getenv("ADMIN_PORTAL_HOME");
    if (configured == null || configured.isBlank() || !Paths.get(configured).isAbsolute()) {
        throw new IOException("Set ADMIN_PORTAL_HOME to an absolute directory owned only by this account.");
    }
    Path dir = Paths.get(configured).normalize();
    if (!Files.exists(dir, LinkOption.NOFOLLOW_LINKS)) {
        Files.createDirectories(dir, PosixFilePermissions.asFileAttribute(
                PosixFilePermissions.fromString("rwx------")));
    }
    if (!Files.isDirectory(dir, LinkOption.NOFOLLOW_LINKS)) {
        throw new IOException("Data directory must be a real directory, not a symbolic link.");
    }
    Path probe = Files.createTempFile(dir, ".owner", ".probe"); // owned by the running account
    try {
        if (!Files.getOwner(dir, LinkOption.NOFOLLOW_LINKS).equals(Files.getOwner(probe))) {
            throw new IOException("Data directory is not owned by the account running the portal.");
        }
    } finally {
        Files.deleteIfExists(probe);
    }
    Set<PosixFilePermission> perms = Files.getPosixFilePermissions(dir, LinkOption.NOFOLLOW_LINKS);
    if (!perms.equals(PosixFilePermissions.fromString("rwx------"))) {
        throw new IOException("Data directory permissions must be rwx------ (owner only).");
    }
    return dir;
}

// AuditLog.record
try (FileChannel channel = FileChannel.open(file, StandardOpenOption.READ, StandardOpenOption.WRITE,
                                            LinkOption.NOFOLLOW_LINKS);
     FileLock lock = channel.lock()) {
```

### SEC-03: Initial `setup` race lets a second unauthenticated first administrator be created
- **Severity:** Medium
- **CWE:** CWE-367: Time-of-check Time-of-use (TOCTOU) Race Condition
